statements.text: The UK-EU summit will take place in Brussels on 20 November. On the table are a food and drink trade deal, progress on emissions trading and linking energy systems, a youth experience scheme and deeper cooperation on immigration. The government says it will work hard over the next five weeks to secure a deal.

The Prime Minister welcomed President Trump's announcement of a reciprocal energy ceasefire. President Zelenskyy has assured him that Ukraine would immediately implement it once a start date is confirmed.

The government assesses that the incident at RAF Fairford is highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran and almost certainly directed by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard. It will crack down on Iran's use of criminal networks, target their funding streams and bring further sanctions to restrict Iran and the IRGC's capacity to do harm.
The Prime Minister has asked Ministers to draw up further sanctions, military support and fiscal packages to provide urgent support in the coming weeks, and is set to tell President Zelenskyy so.

The Prime Minister welcomed President Zelenskyy to Downing Street on 14 October. The leaders said Russia had no interest in peace. The Prime Minister set out the UK's latest package of Lightweight Multirole Missiles and said the UK would continue developing innovative military solutions, including retrofitting British capability onto equipment gifted by other partners, and its diplomatic efforts on international supplies of defensive equipment. The leaders discussed how the UK could accelerate defensive support ahead of winter, including on long-range missiles.

The UK is delivering £45 million of surface-to-air missiles and will accelerate deliveries of British Lightweight Multirole Missiles, which the government says have proven extremely effective against jet-powered drones. It has already committed £1.6 billion to deliver more than 5,000 of these missiles over four years, and will accelerate £10 million of the package to meet Ukraine's most urgent winter requirements.

The government has announced new funding to help Ukraine through its fifth winter under Russian bombardment, and a new sanctions package so that over 90% of Russia's oil producing capacity is now covered by UK sanctions.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said that support for Ukraine is vital for keeping the UK safe, that the UK is with Ukraine for as long as it takes and will go further and faster, and that Russia's aggression cannot be allowed to succeed on the continent.

speakers: Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey
statements.text: Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey will use meetings at the IMF in Bangkok to urge partners to fully implement an equivalent ban on Russian LNG. Healey said he urged partners to back the ban, to curtail the war chest funding Putin.

A UK government spokesperson said the government will continue working with partners to ensure Ukraine has the military and financial support it needs. They said Ukraine has repeatedly shown it is serious about peace while Russia has rejected full and partial ceasefires, and that Russia could end the war today.

A food and drink trade deal is expected to add over £10 billion a year to the UK economy by 2040. It would lift a burden that can reach £1,400 on a single shipment for farmers and food producers, and remove export health certificates that can cost up to £200 each time for small businesses. The proposed energy deal could cut wholesale energy costs in Northern Ireland by 20%.

The Prime Minister said the UK's chances at the summit would be enhanced by being open to discussing the relationship with the EU in the longer term. He said the immediate priority is a successful summit outcome, after which a serious dialogue on the options for the long-term relationship should be set up.

Britain has sent air defence and a Voyager aircraft to Saudi Arabia to provide air-to-air refuelling. A Voyager has already completed 14 operational missions. The Prime Minister condemned the attacks on King Khalid International Airport and said the UK will continue to stand with Saudi Arabia against the Houthis.

Chancellor Merz and the Prime Minister agreed a new partnership to tackle Russian hybrid threats in Europe. The UK will establish a new National Centre for Information Defence. The Prime Minister indicated Britain's openness to Germany joining the Global Combat Air Programme alongside Italy and Japan.

The Prime Minister is making a serious and genuine offer to the Scottish Government to design, together, a new model of regional economic empowerment across Scotland through No10 North and the Scotland Office. Douglas Alexander said the offer is a genuine one and the Scotland Office is ready to work alongside the Scottish Government to make it happen.

The Prime Minister is offering Scotland DWP devolution, a model of localised employment support similar to England's but shaped by Holyrood. The National Economic Council will meet in a couple of weeks with the First Ministers of Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland for the first time since he became Prime Minister, to put the offer on the table.
The Scottish Government has agreed to match the UK government's £10 million to create two defence technical excellence colleges, one in the east and one in the west of Scotland.

The site of Great British Railways' headquarters has been unveiled at Becketwell in Derby. Construction is expected to begin in early 2027 and be completed by spring 2029, with an estimated £151 million boost to the Derby economy and hundreds of rail jobs. Heidi Alexander said Becketwell will become GBR's new home, bringing jobs, investment and opportunity to Derby.

Up to 600 apprentices aged 16 to 21 will enrol over the next four years on the rail foundation apprenticeship, with the first starters based in Derby. Pat McFadden said this is part of a £2.5 billion youth employment support package. Claire Ward said she was particularly pleased about the 600 apprenticeship places.
The UK will take up the G20 presidency in 2027 and place AI centre stage, aiming to agree a single set of global principles and standards on AI during its presidency year.

The Prime Minister raised the Falkland Islands and the clear and declared will of the islanders to remain British with President Trump, and said the UK will always do whatever it takes to uphold their will.

The King has appointed William James Baxter QPM DL as Lord-Lieutenant of County Tyrone, succeeding Sir Robert William Lowry Scott, who retired on 17 June 2026. Baxter was District Commander in Omagh from 1997, including on the day of the Omagh bombing in 1998.
